name: position: static
description: The default positioning value; the element follows normal document flow and offset properties (top/right/bottom/left) have no effect.

name: position: relative
description: Positions an element relative to its normal position in the document flow, using top/right/bottom/left offsets, while still occupying its original space.
notes: Commonly used just to establish a positioning context for an absolutely positioned child, even without offsets.

name: position: absolute
description: Removes an element from normal document flow and positions it relative to its nearest positioned ancestor.
notes: If no ancestor has a position other than static, it positions relative to the initial containing block (the viewport).

name: position: fixed
description: Removes an element from normal flow and positions it relative to the browser viewport, so it stays in place while the page scrolls.
notes: A transformed or filtered ancestor changes the containing block, making a fixed element scroll with that ancestor instead of the viewport.

name: position: sticky
description: Toggles between relative and fixed behavior — the element scrolls normally until it hits a defined offset, then sticks in place within its parent.
notes: Requires a top/bottom/left/right offset to activate, and won't stick past the bounds of its containing block.

name: top / right / bottom / left
description: Sets the offset of a positioned element's edges relative to its containing block.
notes: Has no effect on elements with position: static.

name: z-index
description: Sets the stack order of a positioned element, controlling which overlapping elements appear in front.
notes: Only has an effect on elements with a position value other than static.

name: Stacking context
description: A conceptual grouping created by certain properties (like position + z-index, opacity < 1, or transform) where z-index values only compare against siblings inside the same context.
notes: A high z-index inside a low stacking context can still be visually behind an element with a much lower z-index in a different context.
